layout/arrange_basic.description: Place repeated entities in a grid, radial dial and parametric arch.
walkthrough: Arrange starts with a template and a count. Each layout function computes placements, while forAll permits per-item color or scale changes.
The dial also orients its ticks tangentially. Curve placement uses the returned coordinates; it is not a bounding-box row layout.
experiments: Increase the dial count while keeping radius fixed. Compare spacing, then disable tangent orientation.

layout/arrange_compute_wave.description: Update a dense instance lattice directly through a compute shader.
walkthrough: Arrange with gpu enabled shares a template across a 256-by-256 grid. onCompute supplies WGSL that updates instance data from index and time.

The shader combines traveling waves and a radial component. CPU setup and submission still exist; the scene’s zero-CPU-overhead caption should not be read as a measured end-to-end performance guarantee.
experiments: Reduce both grid dimensions to 64 and isolate one wave term. Inspect its motion before restoring the other terms.

layout/arrange_gpu_demo.description: Render a large instance grid whose transforms are updated from JavaScript.
walkthrough: Arrange with gpu enabled batches repeated circles. Its onUpdate callback still loops through records on the CPU to calculate ripple scaling.
This differs from onCompute, where the calculation runs in WGSL. Instancing reduces repeated geometry and draw submission, but does not automatically move all update work onto the GPU.
experiments: Freeze the onUpdate callback and compare the static grid. Then reduce the count to observe how CPU update workload changes.

layout/feature_layout.description: Arrange a circle grid and align neighboring labels by bounds.
walkthrough: VGroup.arrangeInGrid distributes the circles using their dimensions. nextTo positions a label beside the completed group, and alignTo aligns the side box.
Layout depends on actual bounds. A larger circle can change spacing without any explicit change to the group’s position.
experiments: Double one circle’s radius and rebuild the layout. Inspect neighboring spacing and label placement.

layout/zoom.description: Inspect a live scene through a draggable magnified viewport.
walkthrough: ZoomView receives the scene-content entity and displays a separate view of it. Its focus box selects the source region rather than moving the underlying curve.
Dragging updates focus position, and wheel input changes zoom factor. The moving dot proves that the view mirrors current scene content rather than a static screenshot.
experiments: Drag the focus box over the moving dot, then change zoom factor. Compare magnification with moving the main camera.

modernize/animation_fix.description: Chain entity animations and compare them with grouped animation.
walkthrough: The first play call combines a rectangle transform chain with a circle placement and fill change. Those chains describe animation targets rather than applying all changes immediately.
GroupAnimator applies coordinated animation across several entities. The timing and easing options belong to the animation, while the entities retain their geometry and paint.
experiments: Separate the first parallel play into two awaited calls. Compare the resulting order with the original overlap.

modernize/dynamic_path.description: Populate an initially empty path after the scene has started.
walkthrough: Path begins with no vertices, while a rectangle confirms that ordinary rendering is active. After a wait, setVertices provides path geometry.
The renderer must accommodate the new geometry allocation. This example exercises growth from an empty path rather than merely changing a transform on an existing contour.
experiments: Supply a shorter vertex list first, then a longer one after the second wait. Inspect both updates.

modernize/instance.description: Refresh a spatial vector field through its shared instance representation.
walkthrough: VectorField3D samples the callback over a spatial range. Its arrows share rendering infrastructure instead of requiring separately managed arrow entities for every sample.
updateField refreshes the sampled directions during scene updates. Camera motion changes the viewpoint independently of the field formula.
experiments: Freeze time in the field callback, then orbit the camera. Compare a static field with a changing viewpoint.

modifiers/custom_modifier_demo.description: Implement a contour modifier as a function and as a reusable class.
walkthrough: The functional path resamples its contour before applying a polar warp. The class-based AttractorModifier stores a point, radius and strength, and returns deformed contours.
Changing external variables requires modifier invalidation; property setters in the reusable class can encapsulate that step. Keep the original contour separate from temporary output arrays.
experiments: Reduce attractor radius while keeping strength fixed. Compare localized deformation with changing the functional modifier’s phase.

modifiers/path_modifiers_showcase.description: Combine resampling, displacement, trimming and corner shaping.
walkthrough: Modifiers form an ordered contour pipeline. Resampling gives Wiggle enough points to displace, Trim chooses a visible interval, and RoundCorners changes sharp turns.
The updater changes modifier parameters through retrieved instances. Ordering matters because later modifiers receive the output of earlier ones.
experiments: Move ResampleModifier after WiggleModifier on the wire. Compare the result with the original order.

modifiers/reverse_demo.description: Reverse traversal before revealing a path.
walkthrough: Both rows use the same base curve. ReverseModifier changes the lower contour’s traversal before TrimModifier reveals its interval.
The start and end markers expose the changed direction even when the complete silhouettes match. Reversing traversal differs from reflecting the entity in space.
experiments: Remove ReverseModifier and replay both rows. Compare their reveal direction without changing positions.

modifiers/wiggle_demo.description: Compare smooth and angular displacement along a resampled line.
walkthrough: ResampleModifier supplies enough contour points for WiggleModifier. The two rows use smooth and corner modes with anchored endpoints.
Phase animation changes displacement over time. Seed, frequency and amplitude control different aspects of the noise rather than the line’s overall transform.
experiments: Disable anchorEnds and increase amplitude. Inspect whether the endpoints stay connected to their original positions.

modifiers/wobble_demo.description: Compare single-pass, double-pass and overshooting sketch contours.
walkthrough: WobbleModifier alters contour geometry with hand-drawn irregularity. Separate panels vary passes, corner crossing and endpoint anchoring.
boilFps controls how often the irregularity changes, giving a stepped line-boil effect. Paint sketch effects are additional styling and should be distinguished from displaced contour geometry.
experiments: Set boilFps to zero in one panel. Compare a stable irregular contour with the animated neighboring panel.

modifiers/zigzag_demo.description: Add sharp teeth or smooth waves along a path.
walkthrough: ZigZagModifier displaces the contour along its normals. ridges controls repeated structure; amplitude controls its distance from the original line.
The two styles share the same straight source path. Animation changes modifier settings rather than translating that path.
experiments: Give both rows the same ridges and amplitude. Compare corner and smooth modes alone.

morph_3d/morph_catenoid_helicoid.description: Interpolate sampled members of the catenoid–helicoid associate family.
walkthrough: ParametricModel evaluates each stage using the same parameterization structure. The alpha value selects the mathematical surface before Morph blends between stages.
UI labels name the destination stage while the camera remains interactive. The mathematical isometry concerns the continuous family; finite mesh sampling still limits visual precision.
experiments: Reduce parameter segments and compare the bend with the higher-resolution version. Keep stage alpha values unchanged.

morph_3d/morph_demo.description: Blend a cube and sphere through a MorphModel weight.
walkthrough: The endpoints are ordinary Model entities. MorphModel prepares the chosen matching strategy and exposes a weight that CustomAnimation drives between endpoints.
Weight changes the intermediate geometry; endpoint material settings supply appearance. A reverse weight animation returns to the starting model.
experiments: Stop weight at 0.5 and orbit the camera. Inspect the intermediate silhouette before changing material roughness.

morph_3d/morph_dual_contouring.description: Morph spatial primitives using a volumetric dual-contouring strategy.
walkthrough: The scene cycles between cube, torus and sphere with a shared morph configuration. The volumetric representation allows the transition to differ from direct one-to-one vertex blending.
Dual contouring reconstructs a sampled surface, so resolution and reconstruction settings affect edge fidelity and preparation cost. Rotation exposes intermediate silhouettes.
experiments: Lower the configured resolution and compare cube corners during the transition. Keep easing and duration unchanged.

morph_3d/morph_mobius.description: Change a ribbon’s twist through compatible parameterized stages.
walkthrough: Each ParametricModel samples a ribbon from the same parameter domain. Twist count distinguishes the cylindrical band, Möbius strip and further twisted bands.
Morph interpolates the sampled stages. Some intermediate states can have intersections; a visual interpolation is not a proof that every stage preserves topology.
experiments: Stop the transition halfway between zero and one twist and orbit underneath the ribbon. Inspect intersections and seam behavior.

morph_3d/morph_naive.description: Blend meshes with matching vertex and index layouts.
walkthrough: The sphere mesh provides the shared topology. Other endpoints reuse its index arrangement and deform corresponding vertex positions, making direct interpolation meaningful.
The naive strategy avoids finding correspondence between unrelated meshes. Reordering one endpoint’s vertices would break that correspondence even if its final silhouette still looked correct.
experiments: Change the radial deformation amplitude while retaining vertex order. Compare the midpoint geometry with the endpoint silhouette.

morph_3d/morph_polyhedra.description: Morph several polyhedral forms through a shared sampling scheme.
walkthrough: ParametricModel callbacks describe caps, sides and normals for the cube, tetrahedron, prisms and octahedron. Shared parameter sampling supplies correspondence across the stages.
The formulas, rather than a generic primitive-to-primitive matching step, decide where corresponding points lie. Face-normal choices affect the apparent sharpness of flat regions.
experiments: Change the hexagonal prism’s height while leaving its base radius fixed. Compare corresponding side points during the morph.
